name: moon_sun_clock
_comment: Proves the moon rides §14's warped sun clock rather than the raw one. Latitude 45 / day 37 is
chosen because the moon is exactly full at noon there (tick-derived cycle 0.5000, so the
scenario is not silently testing a gibbous moon) and vanilla's day is 18.06 h against our
physical 14.61 h — a 1.7 h clock gap at each horizon, the largest an ordinary colony sees.
Vanilla's sunset lands at hour 21.03 and sunrise at 2.97.
Every expected value below was computed offline from the same pure cores the mod runs
(MoonMath + SunClockMath + Formulas), including the moon's phase drift across the day.
moon_clock_warp false reproduces the artifact §14 shipped with: sun warped, moon left raw.

steps._comment: Guard against a vacuous run: if this is not a full moon, nothing below means anything.
Midnight is a fixed point of the warp, so both clocks must agree exactly here. This is the control: it proves the change is a time warp and not a blanket offset applied to the moon.
An hour before vanilla's sunset, sun still 7.4 degrees up. On the raw clock the full moon is already in a lit sky; on the warped clock it is still below the horizon, where it belongs.

Vanilla's sunset (21.03) — the instant both shadow patches hand off from sun to moon, and the whole point of the fix. Raw clock: moon 12.8 degrees up, so the moon shadow snaps straight to full strength and moon_shadow_render drops to ~0.75. Warped: moon still below the horizon, no moon shadow yet, so the material stays white.
Just after vanilla's sunrise (2.97). Raw clock leaves the full moon 8.8 degrees up in the morning sky; warped puts it below the horizon.
Deep night, both clocks. The fix must not have simply deleted the moon: it is well up and casting on the warped clock too, so the night stays moonlit.
§14's own contract is untouched by this change: vanilla's sky and our sun still agree about day/night at every hour.
